## 🤖 AI & Tech Industry

The AI industry continues to dominate headlines. **"Anthropic surpasses OpenAI to become most valuable AI startup"** signals a major shift in the competitive landscape, while **"Corporate America Is Starting to Ration AI as Cost Skyrockets"** reveals a growing tension between AI enthusiasm and economic reality. On a more philosophical note, **"Leo's first encyclical attacks technological messianism"** shows that the debate over AI's role in society has now reached the Vatican, with the new Pope weighing in on the dangers of uncritical faith in technology. And the discourse around AI-assisted development continues with **"Vibe Coding Is Not Engineering"**, a pointed critique of treating AI-generated code as a substitute for real software craftsmanship.

---

## 🛠️ Programming & Developer Tools

Developers had plenty to chew on today. The most-discussed post of the day, **"SQLite is all you need for durable workflows"** (599 points, 307 comments), makes a compelling case for using SQLite as the backbone of reliable, long-running processes — a refreshing counterpoint to complex distributed systems. **"Zig: Build System Reworked"** details major improvements to the Zig language's build tooling, exciting the systems programming community. **"Pandoc Templates"** offers a polished resource for document conversion workflows, and **"Openrsync: An implementation of rsync, by the OpenBSD team"** brings a clean, security-focused reimplementation of the classic file-sync utility.

On the hardware and science front, **"IXI's autofocusing lenses are almost ready to replace multifocal glasses"** previews a wearable optics breakthrough that could transform vision correction. **"Floor and Ceil versus Denormals on CPU and GPU"** dives deep into low-level floating-point behavior across processor architectures — essential reading for performance engineers. The interactive **"Navier-Stokes fluid simulation explained with Godot game engine"** makes complex fluid dynamics accessible through a game engine demo, and **"Show HN: Helios"** lets users calculate solar energy potential for any address in Britain, a practical tool for the renewable energy transition.

---

## 🌍 Policy, Society & Curiosities

Rounding out the day, **"Proposed new US funding rules: We can cancel any grant at any time"** (173 points) sparked heated debate about the future of American scientific research, as the OMB moves to give the government sweeping power to pull funding from grants. **"Danish pension fund excludes SpaceX citing governance and valuation"** (323 points) raised eyebrows in the finance world, highlighting concerns about corporate accountability at Elon Musk's rocket company. Finally, **"What Happened to the Locusts?"** — a quirky, high-effort personal investigation — reminded HN readers that curiosity-driven writing still has a proud home on the internet.
